Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

# Why the Moonraker connection skill did not guide the two live Klipper runs (2026-11-04)

Diagnosis only; nothing edited. Runs: openai/gpt-5.4-mini via OpenRouter, build of jusprin-newui at e27c962864. Transcripts as the model saw them: `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cf7649d3-46dd-4047-a831-32851ae18292/scratchpad/report/{moonraker,raspberrypi}-live-chat.md`. The model's web-search results are not in the transcripts (only a "web search" marker), so what it read there is not verifiable.

## The one fact that frames everything: when the skill arrives

The skill is attached to a request only when that request carries the result of a `printer_connect` or `printer_connection_status` call (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3136-3139`), and only once `connection_skill()` knows the host type, which is set by the first connect attempt (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:483-494`). So in both runs the model answered the opening message, added the printer, offered to connect, asked for the address and made the first connect call on the standing prompt alone. The skill's first chance to speak was the reply to "credential_requested". Verified from code and from where "[connect-moonraker skill added here]" sits in both transcripts.

The skill opens with "The rules above still apply." Where the standing prompt gives an exact sentence and the skill gives a fact that contradicts it, the exact sentence won every time (failures 1 and 6 below). The standing prompt is built in `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`.

## Failure by failure

### 1. "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" after the person had already said so (both runs)

What the model saw: the standing prompt's connecting rule, `OFFER_AFTER_ADDING`: "after adding, offer it once: end the reply to a successful printer_add with exactly 'Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?' and then 'Choices: Connect it | Not now'". No condition on whether the person already asked. Both opening messages said "I want to connect it so I can send prints to it." The conduct rule "When the person plainly states what to do ... do it: call the tool without asking again" conflicts, and the literal "exactly" rule won 2 of 2. The skill was not yet in force.
Verified: the model's text matches the prompt's sentence character for character.
Kind of change: standing prompt, not skill. The offer needs an exception for a person who already asked, or the model needs leave to go straight to asking for the address.

### 2. "If you want, I can try that address now" after "can you just try it?" (run 1)

What the model saw, three texts pointing the same way:
- `printer_connect` description (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1631-1632`): "pass only hostType and the address the person gave, and until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this."
- Connecting rule: "ask for the address they open it with in a browser ... then call printer_connect".
- Conduct rule: "When you are guessing ... ask and wait for the person's answer before adding, changing or connecting one."
The 7125 address was the model's own guess, never "the address the person gave", so by those texts it had to ask first even though the person had said "just try it". The skill's "When they want to try again, call printer_connect again with the address to use" does not say whose address counts.
Inferred: consistent with every text the model had; its reasoning is not visible.
Kind of change: tool description and skill. An address the model derived and the person agreed to try is an address to use.

### 3. "Moonraker is there, but it rejected the key" when no key was typed (run 1)

What the model saw: "Connection to Voron 2.4 350 failed: The print host test failed: HTTP 401: {...}". The app's `connect()` has the credential string the form was submitted with (`PrinterConversation.cpp:826-833`) but the note never says whether it was empty. The skill says 401 is "the same answer for no key and for a wrong key" and "wants an API key, or a different one"; nothing told the model which branch it was in, and its own two previous replies had told the person to "type it there", so it assumed a key was typed. Those replies came from the standing rule "When the tool reports credential_requested, say briefly to use that form", which frames the form as something to fill; the skill's "The field can stay empty" (step 3) was in context for the first of them and did not change the wording. The form label itself says "API key (if the printer asks for one)" (`components/PrinterPanel.tsx:187`), but the model never sees the form.
Verified: the note lacks the fact. Inferred: that this is why the model picked "rejected".
Kind of change: app note after a 401 says whether a key was entered. Skill frames 401 for the common case, a person who has no key and does not know what one is.

### 4. Key URL without the port, then "the key isn't exposed that way" (run 1)

What the model saw: its search returned Moonraker's docs, which give `http://{moonraker-host}/access/api_key` with no port. I checked the docs: the port really is omitted there, and 7125 is Moonraker's default. The skill, in step 2 and the "Could not parse" entry, teaches that Moonraker is on 7125 and the Mainsail page is another server, but only as a matter of which address the app needs. It never says that Moonraker's own pages, the key page included, are reached at Moonraker's address and port, the same address that had just answered 401. So the model, having established "8081 is Mainsail, 7125 is Moonraker", handed the person a port-80 URL, a third server. When Chrome could not reach it, the conduct rule "When a guess is ruled out, say so and move to the next one" fit, and the model moved on instead of checking its own URL. At the same moment it called `printer_connect` a third time with nothing changed, against the rule not to repeat a failed step; my reading is that it had no next step left.
Verified: docs omit the port; the skill has no sentence about Moonraker's own pages. Inferred: the causal link.
Kind of change: skill. One sentence that the key page is at Moonraker's address and port, and that a page not reached on a different port says nothing about the key.

### 5. "Mainsail's settings page" / "an API key or access page in Mainsail's settings", never searched (both runs)

What the model saw: skill step 3, "You have not seen where Mainsail or Fluidd show the key, so search for where their version shows it before you say, and ask what they see." The sentence presupposes Mainsail shows the key somewhere. My search found no such place: Mainsail's own "connection unauthorized" FAQ sends people to `trusted_clients` in `moonraker.conf`, and Moonraker's docs give only the `/access/api_key` page and `scripts/fetch-apikey.sh`. So the model filled the skill's premise with a guess, in run 2 without any search since the one at the start of the chat, in run 1 right after two searches that had not shown such a page. The skill handed the model a sentence that says "I don't know; find out", the model found nothing, and the premise survived.
Inferred: that no Mainsail page shows the key is from my search, not from reading Mainsail.
Kind of change: skill. State what is known instead of asking the model to find it: Mainsail and Fluidd do not show the key; the two ways to get it; and that a 401 from a printer on the same home network is most often fixed by adding this computer's network to `trusted_clients`, with no key at all. That is the labelled educated guess a stuck person needs, and the skill has nothing for it.

### 6. "It's connected now, so you can send prints straight to it" while Klipper was shut down or in error (both runs)

What the model saw: the finishing rule, "after the app says the connection is verified ... For example: It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it. You can close this chat now." Both runs reproduce the example almost verbatim. The skill's step 4 says verified "means Moonraker answered, and nothing more: it answered the same way while Klipper could not reach the printer's board", but the skill defers to the rules above it, and the app's note was just "Connection to X verified." The app has the Klipper state: `Moonraker::test` reads `klippy_state` from `/server/info` and only logs it (`src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp:90-99`); the backend turns a pass into "verified" with no detail (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:766-776`). In run 2, asked "is it ready to print right now?", the model answered correctly that it could only see that Moonraker answered, so it had understood the skill; the finishing example had already made it say the opposite.
Verified.
Kind of change: app note carries `klippy_state` (already read); finishing example stops promising sending; or the skill's fact is made a rule that outranks the example.

### 7. The "send a report" card after the second failure, although the 401 was progress (run 1)

What happened: `connection_failed()` shows the card on exactly the second failure of the chat, `++m_failed_connections != 2`, by design ("The rule is the app's, not the model's", `PrinterConversation.cpp:846-860`). It does not look at what failed. The first failure (Mainsail page) and the second (401 from Moonraker) were two different steps, the second further along.
Verified. Not a skill matter.
Kind of change: app rule. Count repeats of the same outcome, or hand the judgement to the model now that it has a skill that says which step each outcome means.

### 8. Generic Klipper kept 250 × 250 although the person said 240 × 225 (run 2)

What the model saw: in add mode the standing prompt has no word about bed size. The scope paragraph that mentions bed size ("A setting the settings tools refuse, such as its bed size, is in its printer settings on this computer") is sent only to change and connect sessions; the settings-tool rules likewise. The finding rules say "Start with just the printer model. Do not ask for nozzle, plate or filament first." The printer list gives each entry's build volume, so the model could see the mismatch, but no tool sets bed size (`printer_add` takes catalogId and nozzle only) and no rule says what to do with a stated size. The model dropped the fact silently.
Verified from `printerInstructions.ts` (`SCOPE`, `SETTINGS` gated on `!adding`).
Kind of change: standing prompt, add mode. Say that a stated bed size is changed manually in the printer's settings after adding, so the person is told rather than ignored.

## What this says about the skill as a whole

- It cannot guide the part of the chat before the first connect call, by construction. Nothing in it reached the opening offer or the address question.
- Where it states a fact that the standing prompt contradicts with an exact sentence (connect offer, finishing line), the prompt wins. The skill's own first line tells the model so.
- Its failure table says which step each outcome means, which is right, but it stops there. For the one place both runs got stuck, a 401 with a person who has no key, it tells the model what it does not know ("You have not seen where ... show the key") and sends it to search. The search returned docs the model misapplied (port) and a premise it filled with a guess (Mainsail settings). What a stuck person needs here is three labelled guesses the skill does not contain: trusted_clients on a home network; the key page at Moonraker's own address and port; the SSH script.
- Two app notes starve it: the 401 note does not say whether a key was entered, and the verified note drops the Klipper state the test already read.

Sources for the two web checks: [Mainsail FAQ: connection unauthorized](https://docs.mainsail.xyz/faq/mainsail_errors/connection-unauthorized/), [Moonraker authorization docs](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/authorization/), [Moonraker installation docs mirror (api_key page, fetch-apikey.sh)](https://server.creatbot.com/Gitea/CreatBot/CreatBotMoonraker/raw/commit/6b45c0c1d81093e27ed1b2d1d15f9bd47d0ec3b5/docs/installation.md).
# Every time the printer chat failed to help someone connect a printer, 31 October to 4 November 2026

Short version, 4 November. Words: the **standing instructions** are what the AI reads in every printer chat. The **extra connection instructions** are added by the app the first time the person tries to connect (the code calls them "skills"); they start with "The rules above still apply", so the standing instructions win a conflict. A **message from the app** is a line the app writes into the chat for the AI, such as "Connection to X failed: HTTP 401". **LAN Only** is the Bambu setting that must be on for JusPrin to connect. The **test program** plays the person from a fixed script and cannot react.

**Run 1, 31 Oct. Kenneth's P1S, LAN Only off, the shipped app.** The app said the plug-in was installed and "the printer can be connected", with no next step, so the AI asked for an address, which is the route for other printer kinds. Asked how to find it, the AI invented menu steps, because the standing instructions demand a location for every question. The app then refused with "no printer in LAN mode is on the network" before it had listened at all, and later hid the P1S it had heard with LAN Only off. The AI repeated the same three options three times, one of them a path the chat does not have, because the standing instructions forced them.

**Run 2, 1 Nov. Same P1S, app fixed to say what it heard, Sonnet.** Outcome right. Three wrong sentences: "didn't find your P1S" seconds before it was heard, because the app's 15-second "found nothing" message read as a result and nothing said a first broadcast takes 8 to 40 s; "the search stops after 15 seconds", made from "a message after 15 seconds"; and "the printer can prepare prints", copied from the app's own words.

**Run 3, 2 Nov morning. First extra instructions, a list of one step per situation. Sonnet, slow P1S.** The line for a failure said: say the app's reason in one sentence, add no cause, tell them to compare the code. With a deliberately wrong code the AI did exactly that twice and had no new idea. With Kenneth's right code it still sent him to compare the code. The real cause, a 28-second login against a plug-in that gives up at 24, was in no message from the app, and the instructions forbade a guess. The app's word "refused" was unsupported.

**Run 4, 2 Nov evening. Rewritten instructions that explain the connection. Sonnet.** With the right code the AI reasoned well ("answered just before the attempt and then went quiet, so I can't tell whether the code was wrong"). But every failure ended in "restart the printer", because the author wrote that untested step in place of the removed one, and with a wrong code the AI never suggested checking the code. The no-printer case went from 5 of 5 to 0 of 3: the rewrite dropped "ask what the screen shows" and had nothing for the moment the app says nothing was found. The AI's notes to itself appeared in the chat. DeepSeek stated "Settings > LAN" as fact. The last two are from the author's report, not read by me.

**Run 5, 2 Nov. Web search only, no extra instructions, Sonnet, healthy P1S.** Zero searches in four chats, with nothing telling the AI to search. With no printer heard it guessed "the printer isn't in LAN mode", wrong for this app, which hears a printer either way; only the removed instructions state that. It gave the code's location as fact in one chat and as a guess in another.

**Run 6, 3 Nov. New Moonraker and OctoPrint instructions, search allowed, Sonnet, test printers in Docker, a scripted person who had the key.** Six of seven connected. The one that did not was the script ignoring a correct guess. "Nothing loaded" came from the standing instructions, which say that for any connected printer. "Mainsail's address is saved" was said before the check. The key page URL was right only because the person had typed Moonraker's port 7125; the instructions never say where Moonraker's pages live. A raw stack trace reached the person.

**Run 7, 4 Nov. Moonraker in Docker needing a key, GPT-5.4 Mini, a person who does not know what an API key is.** "Want to connect it?" after the person had asked to, ordered word for word by the standing instructions. "Please type it there" to someone with no key, from the standing instructions over the extra ones' "can stay empty". "I can try that address now" instead of trying, because the address was the AI's guess and the connect action says to use only the person's address. "It rejected the key" when none was typed, because the app's message does not say whether a key was sent. The key page URL without the port, then "the key isn't exposed that way", because Moonraker's docs omit the port and the instructions never say Moonraker's pages share its port. "Mainsail's settings page" without searching, because the instructions assume Mainsail shows the key; it does not. The report card after a failure that was progress, because the rule only counts to two. "You can send prints straight to it" with Klipper in error, because that sentence is the standing instructions' example of how to finish.

**Run 8, 4 Nov. Kenneth's Pi, no key, Klipper shut down, GPT-5.4 Mini.** The same redundant offer, the same "Mainsail's settings page", the same "send prints straight to it" (followed, when asked, by the correct "I can't see the printer's state"), and a stated 240 × 225 bed dropped without a word, since the standing instructions say nothing about bed size while adding.

The app's `connect()` has the credential string the form was submitted with (`PrinterConversation.cpp:826-833`) but the note never says whether it was empty. The skill says 401 is "the same answer for no key and for a wrong key" and "wants an API key, or a different one"; nothing told the model which branch it was in, and its own two previous replies had told the person to "type it there", so it assumed a key was typed. Those replies came from the standing rule "When the tool reports credential_requested, say briefly to use that form", which frames the form as something to fill; the skill's "The field can stay empty" (step 3) was in context for the first of them and did not change the wording. The form label itself says "API key (if the printer asks for one)" (`components/PrinterPanel.tsx:187`), but the model never sees the form.
Verified: the note lacks the fact. Inferred: that this is why the model picked "rejected".
Kind of change: app note after a 401 says whether a key was entered. Skill frames 401 for the common case, a person who has no key and does not know what one is.

### 4. Key URL without the port, then "the key isn't exposed that way" (run 1)

What the model saw: its search returned Moonraker's docs, which give `http://{moonraker-host}/access/api_key` with no port. I checked the docs: the port really is omitted there, and 7125 is Moonraker's default. The skill, in step 2 and the "Could not parse" entry, teaches that Moonraker is on 7125 and the Mainsail page is another server, but only as a matter of which address the app needs. It never says that Moonraker's own pages, the key page included, are reached at Moonraker's address and port, the same address that had just answered 401. So the model, having established "8081 is Mainsail, 7125 is Moonraker", handed the person a port-80 URL, a third server. When Chrome could not reach it, the conduct rule "When a guess is ruled out, say so and move to the next one" fit, and the model moved on instead of checking its own URL. At the same moment it called `printer_connect` a third time with nothing changed, against the rule not to repeat a failed step; my reading is that it had no next step left.
Verified: docs omit the port; the skill has no sentence about Moonraker's own pages. Inferred: the causal link.
Kind of change: skill. One sentence that the key page is at Moonraker's address and port, and that a page not reached on a different port says nothing about the key.

### 5. "Mainsail's settings page" / "an API key or access page in Mainsail's settings", never searched (both runs)

What the model saw: skill step 3, "You have not seen where Mainsail or Fluidd show the key, so search for where their version shows it before you say, and ask what they see." The sentence presupposes Mainsail shows the key somewhere. My search found no such place: Mainsail's own "connection unauthorized" FAQ sends people to `trusted_clients` in `moonraker.conf`, and Moonraker's docs give only the `/access/api_key` page and `scripts/fetch-apikey.sh`. So the model filled the skill's premise with a guess, in run 2 without any search since the one at the start of the chat, in run 1 right after two searches that had not shown such a page. The skill handed the model a sentence that says "I don't know; find out", the model found nothing, and the premise survived.
Inferred: that no Mainsail page shows the key is from my search, not from reading Mainsail.
Kind of change: skill. State what is known instead of asking the model to find it: Mainsail and Fluidd do not show the key; the two ways to get it; and that a 401 from a printer on the same home network is most often fixed by adding this computer's network to `trusted_clients`, with no key at all. That is the labelled educated guess a stuck person needs, and the skill has nothing for it.

### 6. "It's connected now, so you can send prints straight to it" while Klipper was shut down or in error (both runs)

What the model saw: the finishing rule, "after the app says the connection is verified ... For example: It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it. You can close this chat now." Both runs reproduce the example almost verbatim. The skill's step 4 says verified "means Moonraker answered, and nothing more: it answered the same way while Klipper could not reach the printer's board", but the skill defers to the rules above it, and the app's note was just "Connection to X verified." The app has the Klipper state: `Moonraker::test` reads `klippy_state` from `/server/info` and only logs it (`src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp:90-99`); the backend turns a pass into "verified" with no detail (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:766-776`). In run 2, asked "is it ready to print right now?", the model answered correctly that it could only see that Moonraker answered, so it had understood the skill; the finishing example had already made it say the opposite.
Verified.
Kind of change: app note carries `klippy_state` (already read); finishing example stops promising sending; or the skill's fact is made a rule that outranks the example.

### 7. The "send a report" card after the second failure, although the 401 was progress (run 1)

What happened: `connection_failed()` shows the card on exactly the second failure of the chat, `++m_failed_connections != 2`, by design ("The rule is the app's, not the model's", `PrinterConversation.cpp:846-860`). It does not look at what failed. The first failure (Mainsail page) and the second (401 from Moonraker) were two different steps, the second further along.
Verified. Not a skill matter.
Kind of change: app rule. Count repeats of the same outcome, or hand the judgement to the model now that it has a skill that says which step each outcome means.

### 8. Generic Klipper kept 250 × 250 although the person said 240 × 225 (run 2)

What the model saw: in add mode the standing prompt has no word about bed size. The scope paragraph that mentions bed size ("A setting the settings tools refuse, such as its bed size, is in its printer settings on this computer") is sent only to change and connect sessions; the settings-tool rules likewise. The finding rules say "Start with just the printer model. Do not ask for nozzle, plate or filament first." The printer list gives each entry's build volume, so the model could see the mismatch, but no tool sets bed size (`printer_add` takes catalogId and nozzle only) and no rule says what to do with a stated size. The model dropped the fact silently.
Verified from `printerInstructions.ts` (`SCOPE`, `SETTINGS` gated on `!adding`).
Kind of change: standing prompt, add mode. Say that a stated bed size is changed manually in the printer's settings after adding, so the person is told rather than ignored.

## What this says about the skill as a whole

- It cannot guide the part of the chat before the first connect call, by construction. Nothing in it reached the opening offer or the address question.
- Where it states a fact that the standing prompt contradicts with an exact sentence (connect offer, finishing line), the prompt wins. The skill's own first line tells the model so.
- Its failure table says which step each outcome means, which is right, but it stops there. For the one place both runs got stuck, a 401 with a person who has no key, it tells the model what it does not know ("You have not seen where ... show the key") and sends it to search. The search returned docs the model misapplied (port) and a premise it filled with a guess (Mainsail settings). What a stuck person needs here is three labelled guesses the skill does not contain: trusted_clients on a home network; the key page at Moonraker's own address and port; the SSH script.
- Two app notes starve it: the 401 note does not say whether a key was entered, and the verified note drops the Klipper state the test already read.

Sources for the two web checks: [Mainsail FAQ: connection unauthorized](https://docs.mainsail.xyz/faq/mainsail_errors/connection-unauthorized/), [Moonraker authorization docs](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/authorization/), [Moonraker installation docs mirror (api_key page, fetch-apikey.sh)](https://server.creatbot.com/Gitea/CreatBot/CreatBotMoonraker/raw/commit/6b45c0c1d81093e27ed1b2d1d15f9bd47d0ec3b5/docs/installation.md).
# Every time the printer chat failed to help someone connect a printer, 31 October to 4 November 2026

Short version, 4 November. Words: the **standing instructions** are what the AI reads in every printer chat. The **extra connection instructions** are added by the app the first time the person tries to connect (the code calls them "skills"); they start with "The rules above still apply", so the standing instructions win a conflict. A **message from the app** is a line the app writes into the chat for the AI, such as "Connection to X failed: HTTP 401". **LAN Only** is the Bambu setting that must be on for JusPrin to connect. The **test program** plays the person from a fixed script and cannot react.

**Run 1, 31 Oct. Kenneth's P1S, LAN Only off, the shipped app.** The app said the plug-in was installed and "the printer can be connected", with no next step, so the AI asked for an address, which is the route for other printer kinds. Asked how to find it, the AI invented menu steps, because the standing instructions demand a location for every question. The app then refused with "no printer in LAN mode is on the network" before it had listened at all, and later hid the P1S it had heard with LAN Only off. The AI repeated the same three options three times, one of them a path the chat does not have, because the standing instructions forced them.

**Run 2, 1 Nov. Same P1S, app fixed to say what it heard, Sonnet.** Outcome right. Three wrong sentences: "didn't find your P1S" seconds before it was heard, because the app's 15-second "found nothing" message read as a result and nothing said a first broadcast takes 8 to 40 s; "the search stops after 15 seconds", made from "a message after 15 seconds"; and "the printer can prepare prints", copied from the app's own words.

**Run 3, 2 Nov morning. First extra instructions, a list of one step per situation. Sonnet, slow P1S.** The line for a failure said: say the app's reason in one sentence, add no cause, tell them to compare the code. With a deliberately wrong code the AI did exactly that twice and had no new idea. With Kenneth's right code it still sent him to compare the code. The real cause, a 28-second login against a plug-in that gives up at 24, was in no message from the app, and the instructions forbade a guess. The app's word "refused" was unsupported.

**Run 4, 2 Nov evening. Rewritten instructions that explain the connection. Sonnet.** With the right code the AI reasoned well ("answered just before the attempt and then went quiet, so I can't tell whether the code was wrong"). But every failure ended in "restart the printer", because the author wrote that untested step in place of the removed one, and with a wrong code the AI never suggested checking the code. The no-printer case went from 5 of 5 to 0 of 3: the rewrite dropped "ask what the screen shows" and had nothing for the moment the app says nothing was found. The AI's notes to itself appeared in the chat. DeepSeek stated "Settings > LAN" as fact. The last two are from the author's report, not read by me.

**Run 5, 2 Nov. Web search only, no extra instructions, Sonnet, healthy P1S.** Zero searches in four chats, with nothing telling the AI to search. With no printer heard it guessed "the printer isn't in LAN mode", wrong for this app, which hears a printer either way; only the removed instructions state that. It gave the code's location as fact in one chat and as a guess in another.

**Run 6, 3 Nov. New Moonraker and OctoPrint instructions, search allowed, Sonnet, test printers in Docker, a scripted person who had the key.** Six of seven connected. The one that did not was the script ignoring a correct guess. "Nothing loaded" came from the standing instructions, which say that for any connected printer. "Mainsail's address is saved" was said before the check. The key page URL was right only because the person had typed Moonraker's port 7125; the instructions never say where Moonraker's pages live. A raw stack trace reached the person.

**Run 7, 4 Nov. Moonraker in Docker needing a key, GPT-5.4 Mini, a person who does not know what an API key is.** "Want to connect it?" after the person had asked to, ordered word for word by the standing instructions. "Please type it there" to someone with no key, from the standing instructions over the extra ones' "can stay empty". "I can try that address now" instead of trying, because the address was the AI's guess and the connect action says to use only the person's address. "It rejected the key" when none was typed, because the app's message does not say whether a key was sent. The key page URL without the port, then "the key isn't exposed that way", because Moonraker's docs omit the port and the instructions never say Moonraker's pages share its port. "Mainsail's settings page" without searching, because the instructions assume Mainsail shows the key; it does not. The report card after a failure that was progress, because the rule only counts to two. "You can send prints straight to it" with Klipper in error, because that sentence is the standing instructions' example of how to finish.

**Run 8, 4 Nov. Kenneth's Pi, no key, Klipper shut down, GPT-5.4 Mini.** The same redundant offer, the same "Mainsail's settings page", the same "send prints straight to it" (followed, when asked, by the correct "I can't see the printer's state"), and a stated 240 × 225 bed dropped without a word, since the standing instructions say nothing about bed size while adding.

358	## Errors should teach the next valid call
359	
360	When an invalid state is expected, handle it with ordinary control flow and return a structured error. Do not throw an exception. An error should say what the problem is and include only the data the Agent needs to correct the call.
361	
362	An error is judged by four things, in this order:
363	
364	1. **It says truthfully what happened, including whether anything changed.** A failed call changed nothing, unless its message says what it had already changed when it stopped. A tool that can stop part-way says so in its message (`printer_setup` names the printer it already selected and the edits it dropped; `object_repair` names the paint it removed and the parts it repaired). Prefer checking everything before changing anything, so that a refusal never comes part-way: `plate_layout` checks the plate limit, copies of a disabled object, and an open editing tool before it applies any row.
365	2. **It names the next step and who takes it,** through its code (below) and its message.
366	3. **The same situation gets the same code from every tool.** A plate id that is not in the open project is `not_found` from `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`, `export_file`, `plate_layout`, `project_delete_items` and the import tools.
367	4. **A broken invariant is not reported to the model.** A state the code guarantees cannot happen (a tool with no handler, a coordinator without the product state every app host gives it, a checked id that does not parse) throws, so it reaches Sentry.
368	
369	Every code a tool can fail with is listed in `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`, and `ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail` throws on any other. The in-app agent and MCP clients read the same codes: the MCP adapter passes them through unchanged. Each code stands for one next step:
370	
371	| Next step | Codes |
372	|---|---|
373	| Fix the arguments and call again | `invalid_arguments`, `unknown_tool`, `unknown_skill`; the settings codes in "Error codes" below; the printer chats' own codes |
374	| Decide again: not run, because an earlier call of the same response failed (in-app only) | `not_run` |
375	| Read the state again, then call again | `not_found` (an id that is not in the open project), `stale_workspace` (the project changed since the read the call was based on), `feature_expired` (a face, edge or hole handle from an earlier revision), `connection_lost` (MCP bridge only: the outcome is unknown) |
376	| Wait, then call again | `busy` |
377	| Do the step the message names first | `needs_step` |
378	| Ask the person | `opened_before`, `workspace_unavailable` (no open project, or no FFF printer selected) |
379	| Stop and tell the person | `refused` (OrcaSlicer does not do this here), `failed` (OrcaSlicer tried and failed), `local_save_failed`, `cancelled` |
380	
381	The adapter decides the kind, because only it knows whether OrcaSlicer was busy, refused, or failed: `WorkspaceError` has a kind for each code (`NotFound`, `StaleId`, `Busy`, `NeedsStep`, `Refused`, `Failed`, `WorkspaceUnavailable`, `InvalidArgument`, `FeatureExpired`, `StaleSettings`), and the coordinator maps each one to its code in one function. Every `stale_workspace` carries the expected and the current session and revision in its details. Protocol errors at the transport level are separate JSON-RPC errors.
382	
383	A new failure picks the code whose next step fits. Add a code only for a next step none of these describe, and add it to `ToolErrors.hpp` and to this table together. The project prompt names no codes: a code and its message explain themselves. The MCP server instructions summarize the table above for external clients.
384	
385	The settings tools return these correction details, each limited in size:
386	
387	- unknown setting: the canonical code `unknown_setting`, the original key, and a short `suggestions` list;
388	- invalid enum value: the key, a diagnostic message, and the valid values in `allowed`;
389	- value out of range: the key, a diagnostic message, and the `min`/`max` bounds. Units are available from the setting's metadata;
390	- incompatible settings: the keys that conflict, and OrcaSlicer's reason;
391	- stale call: the expected and the current session/revision, plus an instruction to read again;
392	- unavailable operation: the requested scope has no active preset or target.
393	
394	A failure that should be impossible (a broken invariant) must stay visible to diagnostics and to Sentry. Catch an error at the boundary between two layers only to recover from it, to translate a known error, or to add context that is essential.
395	
396	### A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result
397	
398	Added 2026-11-01, narrowed 2026-11-02. On 2026-10-31 a Bambu Lab P1S failed to connect through the printer chat: the person gave its address, the app had heard the printer in cloud mode, and the result said "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now". The right next step, turning LAN Only on, was in the app's hands and in nobody else's. The four rules above are about the code; this one is about the person on the other side of the model:
399	
400	**A refusal or an empty result is wrong when it leaves a person stuck: told something false or useless at that moment, with the right next step hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call.**
401	
402	That is the whole test, and it is applied per case, not per code shape. A sweep on 2026-11-01 found eleven places where a result said less than the app knew. Judged by this test, three were real and were fixed; the other eight were not, and their fixes were taken out again (Kenneth, 2026-11-02: "fixing a non-problem is a lot worse than not fixing a real problem"). The model recovering the truth with its next ordinary call (`slice_report` after a bare `valid: false`, a search without a scope after an empty page) is not a stuck person, and every field added for such a case is text every model reads on every call. The three that were real:
403	
404	1. **A wrong Bambu access code.** Upstream's handler erases the saved code and clears the selection; a backend that read the selection said "The selected printer changed" or "The printer is no longer available", and the person, who had mistyped the code from the printer's screen, was sent to refresh a list. `Printers/ConnectionEvents` records the plug-in's answer at the moment it arrives, and the backend reads that before it reads the selection.
405	2. **A print host that answered.** A Klipper owner who types the Mainsail port instead of Moonraker's, or picks Moonraker for an OctoPrint host, was told "Could not reach the print host. Check its address, API key and network." The host was reached and said what it was. One line of the host's own answer travels with the failure.
406	3. **A heard printer the connection does not offer.** A person retrying after a failed add, with the printer's serial already linked to the first saved entry, was told "no printer of this model is on the network" while it was being heard. Every printer the search heard is in `seen` with a `reason` (`other_model`, `linked_elsewhere`, `other_device`, `occupied`, `cloud_mode`, `account_only`), and the refusal names it.
407	
408	What they share: the fork read what OrcaSlicer's event left behind (a cleared selection, a pass-or-fail flag, a filtered list) instead of the event itself, and the fakes could not produce the failing answer, so no test ever showed the sentence a person would read. The guard for a case that passes the test is a state table: arrange each state, read the tools that report it, and assert the results differ (`tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", the `--printer-setup` harness checks named `*_are_told_apart`), with the fake taught to produce every failure the real owner can (`FakeBambuAgent::fail_next_connect`, the harness's `StandInHost` with a status and body). Where a table deliberately leaves two states reading the same, a one-line comment at that assertion says why. Kenneth's rule of 2026-10-15 stands as it was: a rare failure the app has nothing more to say about gets one generic error.
409	
410	### How to fix a result that hides the failure
411	
412	Added 2026-11-02. The fix is mechanical, and a new check is almost never part of it. Four rules, in order (Kenneth, 2026-11-02):
413	
414	1. **The source gives an error: forward it.** Pass on the `what()`, the reason string or the list the code already holds, and keep any instruction the sentence carried, such as "Do not repeat the call".
415	2. **The source gives nothing: say what the code tested or saw, and delete any guessed cause.** Do not add a check or a branch to tell causes apart. If the code does not know something, the sentence stops claiming it, and there is nothing further to investigate.
416	3. **A comment says a lower layer's message misleads the model: keep the replacement.** `generate_calibration` drops the load report on purpose, because the over-the-build-volume warning is about the test model before the generator cut it. A replacement with no such comment is not protected by this rule.
417	4. **The fix needs a file OrcaSlicer owns: skip the entry.** Kenneth approves any upstream change one by one.
418	
419	A forwarded error reaches the model, so it must not name Orca or OrcaSlicer, and `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` does not see those strings.
420	
421	False successes are the exception to rule 1, because the source reports nothing. These OrcaSlicer calls do not say when they failed, so check the outcome yourself:
422	
423	- `store_stl` always returns true. `TriangleMesh::write_binary` returns false only when the file will not open, so a full disk shows only in the file size (84 + 50 per facet).
424	- `PresetBundle::export_current_configs` lists a file whether or not it was written.
425	- `Plater::split_object` returns nothing and only shows a dialog, and the model is unchanged.
426	- `ModelObject::split` splits a multi-volume object only by volume, so one solid part with a modifier stays whole however many shells it has.
427	
428	## Read, mutation, and destructive policy
429

1. **It says truthfully what happened, including whether anything changed.** A failed call changed nothing, unless its message says what it had already changed when it stopped. A tool that can stop part-way says so in its message (`printer_setup` names the printer it already selected and the edits it dropped; `object_repair` names the paint it removed and the parts it repaired). Prefer checking everything before changing anything, so that a refusal never comes part-way: `plate_layout` checks the plate limit, copies of a disabled object, and an open editing tool before it applies any row.
2. **It names the next step and who takes it,** through its code (below) and its message.
3. **The same situation gets the same code from every tool.** A plate id that is not in the open project is `not_found` from `slice_start`, `slice_report`, `slice_inspect`, `view_render`, `export_file`, `plate_layout`, `project_delete_items` and the import tools.
4. **A broken invariant is not reported to the model.** A state the code guarantees cannot happen (a tool with no handler, a coordinator without the product state every app host gives it, a checked id that does not parse) throws, so it reaches Sentry.

Every code a tool can fail with is listed in `Agent/ToolErrors.hpp`, and `ToolExecutionCoordinator::fail` throws on any other. The in-app agent and MCP clients read the same codes: the MCP adapter passes them through unchanged. Each code stands for one next step:

| Next step | Codes |
|---|---|
| Fix the arguments and call again | `invalid_arguments`, `unknown_tool`, `unknown_skill`; the settings codes in "Error codes" below; the printer chats' own codes |
| Decide again: not run, because an earlier call of the same response failed (in-app only) | `not_run` |
| Read the state again, then call again | `not_found` (an id that is not in the open project), `stale_workspace` (the project changed since the read the call was based on), `feature_expired` (a face, edge or hole handle from an earlier revision), `connection_lost` (MCP bridge only: the outcome is unknown) |
| Wait, then call again | `busy` |
| Do the step the message names first | `needs_step` |
| Ask the person | `opened_before`, `workspace_unavailable` (no open project, or no FFF printer selected) |
| Stop and tell the person | `refused` (OrcaSlicer does not do this here), `failed` (OrcaSlicer tried and failed), `local_save_failed`, `cancelled` |

The adapter decides the kind, because only it knows whether OrcaSlicer was busy, refused, or failed: `WorkspaceError` has a kind for each code (`NotFound`, `StaleId`, `Busy`, `NeedsStep`, `Refused`, `Failed`, `WorkspaceUnavailable`, `InvalidArgument`, `FeatureExpired`, `StaleSettings`), and the coordinator maps each one to its code in one function. Every `stale_workspace` carries the expected and the current session and revision in its details. Protocol errors at the transport level are separate JSON-RPC errors.

A new failure picks the code whose next step fits. Add a code only for a next step none of these describe, and add it to `ToolErrors.hpp` and to this table together. The project prompt names no codes: a code and its message explain themselves. The MCP server instructions summarize the table above for external clients.

The settings tools return these correction details, each limited in size:

- unknown setting: the canonical code `unknown_setting`, the original key, and a short `suggestions` list;
- invalid enum value: the key, a diagnostic message, and the valid values in `allowed`;
- value out of range: the key, a diagnostic message, and the `min`/`max` bounds. Units are available from the setting's metadata;
- incompatible settings: the keys that conflict, and OrcaSlicer's reason;
- stale call: the expected and the current session/revision, plus an instruction to read again;
- unavailable operation: the requested scope has no active preset or target.

A failure that should be impossible (a broken invariant) must stay visible to diagnostics and to Sentry. Catch an error at the boundary between two layers only to recover from it, to translate a known error, or to add context that is essential.

### A reason travels with every refusal and every empty result

Added 2026-11-01, narrowed 2026-11-02. On 2026-10-31 a Bambu Lab P1S failed to connect through the printer chat: the person gave its address, the app had heard the printer in cloud mode, and the result said "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now". The right next step, turning LAN Only on, was in the app's hands and in nobody else's. The four rules above are about the code; this one is about the person on the other side of the model:

**A refusal or an empty result is wrong when it leaves a person stuck: told something false or useless at that moment, with the right next step hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call.**

That is the whole test, and it is applied per case, not per code shape. A sweep on 2026-11-01 found eleven places where a result said less than the app knew. Judged by this test, three were real and were fixed; the other eight were not, and their fixes were taken out again (Kenneth, 2026-11-02: "fixing a non-problem is a lot worse than not fixing a real problem"). The model recovering the truth with its next ordinary call (`slice_report` after a bare `valid: false`, a search without a scope after an empty page) is not a stuck person, and every field added for such a case is text every model reads on every call. The three that were real:

1. **A wrong Bambu access code.** Upstream's handler erases the saved code and clears the selection; a backend that read the selection said "The selected printer changed" or "The printer is no longer available", and the person, who had mistyped the code from the printer's screen, was sent to refresh a list. `Printers/ConnectionEvents` records the plug-in's answer at the moment it arrives, and the backend reads that before it reads the selection.
2. **A print host that answered.** A Klipper owner who types the Mainsail port instead of Moonraker's, or picks Moonraker for an OctoPrint host, was told "Could not reach the print host. Check its address, API key and network." The host was reached and said what it was. One line of the host's own answer travels with the failure.
3. **A heard printer the connection does not offer.** A person retrying after a failed add, with the printer's serial already linked to the first saved entry, was told "no printer of this model is on the network" while it was being heard. Every printer the search heard is in `seen` with a `reason` (`other_model`, `linked_elsewhere`, `other_device`, `occupied`, `cloud_mode`, `account_only`), and the refusal names it.

What they share: the fork read what OrcaSlicer's event left behind (a cleared selection, a pass-or-fail flag, a filtered list) instead of the event itself, and the fakes could not produce the failing answer, so no test ever showed the sentence a person would read. The guard for a case that passes the test is a state table: arrange each state, read the tools that report it, and assert the results differ (`tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", the `--printer-setup` harness checks named `*_are_told_apart`), with the fake taught to produce every failure the real owner can (`FakeBambuAgent::fail_next_connect`, the harness's `StandInHost` with a status and body). Where a table deliberately leaves two states reading the same, a one-line comment at that assertion says why. Kenneth's rule of 2026-10-15 stands as it was: a rare failure the app has nothing more to say about gets one generic error.

### How to fix a result that hides the failure

Added 2026-11-02. The fix is mechanical, and a new check is almost never part of it. Four rules, in order (Kenneth, 2026-11-02):

1. **The source gives an error: forward it.** Pass on the `what()`, the reason string or the list the code already holds, and keep any instruction the sentence carried, such as "Do not repeat the call".
2. **The source gives nothing: say what the code tested or saw, and delete any guessed cause.** Do not add a check or a branch to tell causes apart. If the code does not know something, the sentence stops claiming it, and there is nothing further to investigate.
3. **A comment says a lower layer's message misleads the model: keep the replacement.** `generate_calibration` drops the load report on purpose, because the over-the-build-volume warning is about the test model before the generator cut it. A replacement with no such comment is not protected by this rule.
4. **The fix needs a file OrcaSlicer owns: skip the entry.** Kenneth approves any upstream change one by one.

A forwarded error reaches the model, so it must not name Orca or OrcaSlicer, and `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` does not see those strings.

False successes are the exception to rule 1, because the source reports nothing. These OrcaSlicer calls do not say when they failed, so check the outcome yourself:

- `store_stl` always returns true. `TriangleMesh::write_binary` returns false only when the file will not open, so a full disk shows only in the file size (84 + 50 per facet).
- `PresetBundle::export_current_configs` lists a file whether or not it was written.
- `Plater::split_object` returns nothing and only shows a dialog, and the model is unchanged.
- `ModelObject::split` splits a multi-volume object only by volume, so one solid part with a modifier stays whole however many shells it has.

commit 8dbada1cc634391e30bb30c5a036839b11e2841c
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 3 08:16:46 2026 -0800

    Make tool results tell the model the truth about what the app observed
    
    On 2026-10-31 a person could not connect a Bambu P1S through the printer chat.
    The app's log shows printer_connect refused with "No printer in LAN mode is on
    the network now" before any search had started, and again after the printer
    had announced itself in cloud mode. The app had observed each of these states
    and reported none of them. A sweep of every tool result on 2026-11-01 found
    more places where a result said less than the app knew, or stated a cause the
    code had not checked. This commit fixes the ones that leave a person stuck and
    writes down the rule the rest are held to.
    
    The rule (Agent/ToolErrors.hpp and the tool guide, agent-docs/jusprin/
    mcp-tool-extension-guide.md): a result is fixed only when a person who
    plausibly exists was told something false or useless at that moment, with the
    right next step hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call. Of the eleven
    sweep findings, three pass that test and stay. The other eight were taken out
    again with their guards and fakes, because fixing a non-problem is worse than
    leaving a real one. The guide's new section says how to fix a result that
    hides a failure: forward the error the source gives; if it gives none, say
    what the code tested or saw; keep a replacement that a comment defends; skip
    anything that needs an OrcaSlicer file. It also lists the OrcaSlicer calls that
    do not report failure (for example store_stl always returns true), and warns
    that a forwarded error reaches the model and the wording test does not see it.
    
    Bambu network search, in the printer conversation:
    - printer_connect no longer claims what was not checked. It says that no
      search has run, or how long it has run, or what it has seen.
    - printer_connection_status returns the search state, because its first read
      is empty by construction, and lists the printers it cannot offer in a "seen"
      list with name, address and reason, apart from the connectable candidates.
      printer_connect names such a printer when asked for it by id, name or
      address. The reasons are cloud mode, another model, linked to another saved
      printer, a different device of this model, and occupied.
    - A note starts a turn when the first printer appears and after 15 seconds
      with none. A printer known only from the Bambu account is reported as
      account_only and never as seen on the network, so people on Bambu's cloud
      are not interrupted.
    - After 15 seconds with nothing found the app checks who holds UDP port 2021,
      where Bambu printers announce themselves, and reports port_taken or
      not_listening. The network plug-in binds the port only as the app starts, so
      both texts ask for a restart. Checked against a real P1S with the port free,
      held throughout and let go during the search. Windows reports nothing and is
      untested; the Linux path has not been run.
    
    The three fixes kept from the sweep:
    - The plug-in's answer to a connect attempt is recorded and read before the
      selection, so a wrong access code is no longer reported as a vanished
      printer. The recording is one added line in GUI_App.cpp (see below).
    - The print host's own answer travels with a failed host test, bounded to one
      line: "HTTP 401: ...", "does not look like Moonraker", curl's reason.
    - Every heard printer is kept in "seen" with its reason, so a retry after a
      failed add no longer reads as "no printer of this model".
    
    Other results that were false, each reproduced against the real app first:
    - Splitting an object that has one solid part and a modifier into objects did
      nothing and reported success with the project's last object as the piece.

Any other that is a task of its own, as that section defines one (work that lands apart from this change, something the user set aside earlier, or a self-contained next task better started fresh than from a long history — never work unrelated to the request), you propose with `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` (initiation "own_initiative"; skip if you already did this turn); it shows as a New task card in the transcript, where the user starts it.

<browsers>
You have two browsers in this session:
- The built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser": a browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the user's Chrome. The built-in browser is the default for this session and its tools are already loaded, so use it unless the user asks for Claude in Chrome.
- Claude in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`), also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser: the user's real Chrome. Use it when the user asks for it by any of these names or by describing it.
A browser is unavailable only when none of its tools are in this session (neither loaded nor deferred) or its tool calls cannot reach the browser; a blocked site, a declined approval, or a sign-in page does not make a browser unavailable. If the user asks for one browser by name and it is unavailable, say so and ask before using the other one. When a sign-in page comes up, stay in that browser; if the user says they cannot sign in to a site in the built-in browser, offer Claude in Chrome and switch only if they agree.
</browsers>

<built_in_browser>
You have a built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser or the browser pane: a real browser with tabs inside the Claude desktop app, isolated from the user's Chrome, with its tools already loaded. You can use it for web research, reading pages and docs, checking staging or a deployed app, filling forms, and previewing this project's dev servers. `preview_start` with a `url` opens a site in its own tab; prefer `get_page_text` / `read_page` over screenshots for reading. The user sees the same pane and can take over; they may be asked to allow a site first, and if a site is refused or declined, tell them and move on rather than retrying. Treat any sign-ins there as the user's: never sign out, change credentials, or act on an account beyond what the task needs.
</built_in_browser>

<simulator_tools>
When the user wants to run, test, or visually check an iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?"), use mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control. Simulators and emulators only — when the user asks to run on their physical device ("on my phone", "on my device"), build for the device with your normal build tools instead; these tools and the panel cannot drive a real device. Open the live panel ('attach') whenever the user would want to see the app themselves — and call 'attach' FIRST, before you build or launch: it is cheap, it opens instantly on a booted device (and surfaces the one-time device-access prompt while the user is still at the keyboard), and if nothing is booted it returns a harmless, clear error — boot or build first in that case, then attach as soon as a device is up. Do not defer the panel to the implicit re-attach in 'launch'; the panel should already be open while you build. The panel is the user's view; your own verification (screenshot, tap, text) is headless and works without it — verify yourself rather than asking the user to check. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. If 'attach' fails, follow the error's remediation: address the cause (for example no booted device, or device access not granted) or tell the user — don't retry the same call in a loop unless the error says retrying will work. If the failure is the host's Xcode setup (a wrong xcode-select, missing Xcode, or a missing iOS platform), tell the user right away with the exact fix the error gives — most of these fixes need their password, so you cannot run them (the error itself says when a fix is one you can run) — and if you continue by driving the Simulator app with generic screen tools instead, say so explicitly; never switch silently. An app in the iOS Simulator reaches a server on the machine your shell runs on at localhost, with no port forwarding.
</simulator_tools>

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default.
